summary_md:
**[@cv_usk](https://x.com/cv_usk/status/2115241134146363564)** walks through **"Is Complex Agentic Memory Always Needed? Naive RAG Is Stronger Than We Thought."**

- The baseline ("Raw-RAG") just windows conversations into 256-token chunks, embeds, retrieves 128, cross-encoder-reranks to 15 — no LLM extraction, summaries or graphs.
- It ranks first among memory systems in 6 of 7 settings (e.g. 48.32 vs Memora's 43.84 on MemoryAgentBench) and ingests ~1M tokens in ~0.33 h vs ~27 h.
- The paper attributes gaps to *evidence delivery*: atomic-fact extraction cost ~19.6 points; summaries and graph expansion ~6 points each.

referenced_urls.title: Is Complex Agentic Memory Always Needed? Naive RAG Is Stronger Than We Thought

relevance: A strong reality check for agent memory design: raw evidence plus good retrieval may beat elaborate memory pipelines.
